routes.name: Electronic Travel Authorization (eTA)
routes.summary: If you're from a visa-exempt country and you fly to Canada, you need an eTA. It's a quick online form. You don't need one if you arrive by land or sea.

other: Valid passport from a visa-exempt country or territory, and an email address.
Not needed for US citizens, US lawful permanent residents, or Canadian citizens and permanent residents.
Some passports have extra rules, for example Israel (national passport), Romania (electronic passport), Taiwan (passport with personal ID number).
Stateless people and holders of refugee travel documents need a visa, not an eTA.
The official visa-exempt country list is on the check-visa-eta page.

stay.note: Visitors are normally allowed to stay up to 6 months. The officer at the border can set a shorter or longer stay. eTA validity period was not stated on the pages read.

steps: Have your passport and payment card ready.
Fill in the online form (it can't be saved).
Pay the fee.
Check your email for the result.
routes.processing: Most applications are approved within minutes. If documents are needed, instructions are emailed within 72 hours.

routes.name: US citizens and US permanent residents (no visa or eTA)
routes.summary: US citizens and US green card holders don't need a visa or an eTA to visit or transit Canada. Bring a valid passport, and a green card for permanent residents.

other: US lawful permanent residents flying in need a valid passport from their country plus proof of US status.
US citizens without a passport can travel by land or sea (not air) with documents showing name, date of birth and citizenship, but IRCC recommends carrying a passport.

sources.label: Check if you need a visa or eTA

routes.name: eTA instead of a visa for some visa-required nationals
routes.summary: Some citizens of normally visa-required countries, such as Brazil, Mexico, Thailand and Uruguay, can apply for an eTA instead of a visa if they meet certain conditions and fly in. IRCC also lists Indonesia and Malaysia from May 26, 2026.

other: Extra conditions apply (IRCC says 'certain requirements'). Check the official tool for your passport.
Only valid for air travel. By land or sea you need a visitor visa.
The country list on the pages read says 'such as', so it may not be complete.

sources.label: Check if you need a visa or eTA

routes.name: Visitor Visa (Temporary Resident Visa)
routes.summary: A visa for visa-required nationals to visit Canada for tourism, family visits, business or similar. It can be valid up to 10 years, or until your passport expires.

other: Needed if your passport is on the visa-required list.
Tourists should show an invitation letter if visiting someone, travel history, an itinerary, 6 months of bank statements and an employer letter.
Passport valid at least 6 months past your planned travel date.

stay.note: Visa can be issued for up to 10 years or until your passport or biometrics expire, whichever is first. Each stay is normally up to 6 months, set by the border officer.

steps: Gather your documents.
Apply through the IRCC Portal and pay the fees.
Book your biometrics appointment if told to.

fees.label: Biometrics per person
fees.note: Up to 170 CAD for a family, if eligible.

sources.label: Apply for a visitor visa
eTA: After you apply (length of stay)

routes.name: Business Visitor
routes.summary: Short business trips like meetings, conferences, trade fairs and training don't need a work permit. You still need an eTA or visitor visa depending on your passport.

other: Stay under 6 months.
You won't enter the Canadian labour market.
Your main business, income and profits are based outside Canada.
Allowed: buying goods or services, taking orders, attending meetings and trade fairs, after-sales service under a warranty, and receiving or giving training.
US and Mexican nationals have extra allowed activities under CUSMA.

stay.note: Under 6 months, typically a few days or weeks.

sources.label: Business visitors: eligibility

routes.name: Remote work as a visitor (no digital nomad visa)
routes.summary: Canada has no digital nomad visa. An IRCC briefing note says nomads who aren't entering the Canadian labour market can enter as visitors and stay up to six months, working for themselves or foreign employers.

other: Source is a 2023 parliamentary committee briefing, not a dedicated program page. Confirm with IRCC before relying on it.
You need a valid eTA or visitor visa for your passport.
If you find a Canadian employer you may apply for a work permit.

sources.label: IRCC briefing: Tech Talent Strategy and digital nomads

routes.name: Transit through Canada
routes.summary: What you need to transit depends on your passport and how you travel. eTA-required travelers need an eTA to transit by air. Visa-required travelers need a transit visa or visitor visa unless a no-visa transit program applies.

other: Transit visa: for visa-required nationals connecting between two international flights (or on a flight that stops in Canada), staying 48 hours or less, without a visitor visa and not eligible for an eTA.
Visitor visa needed if you stay more than 48 hours, or cross by bus, car, train, boat or cruise ship.
eTA is not needed to transit by train, bus, boat or cruise ship.
Passport holders of China, Indonesia, the Philippines, Thailand and Taiwan (passports with a personal ID number) may transit without a visa if they meet conditions.
US citizens and permanent residents can transit without a visa by any mode.

stay.note: Transit visa is for transit of 48 hours or less.

sources.label: Transit through Canada

routes.name: Express Entry: Canadian Experience Class
routes.summary: Permanent residence for skilled workers with Canadian work experience. You enter the Express Entry pool and need an invitation to apply. No job offer or education requirement.

eligibility.language: CLB 7 for TEER 0 or 1 jobs, CLB 5 for TEER 2 or 3 jobs
other: One year of eligible Canadian work experience in the last 3 years.
No proof of funds needed.
A provincial nomination adds 600 points to your ranking.

steps: Check you qualify for a program.
Create an Express Entry profile.
Get invited in a round of invitations.
Submit your permanent residence application.

routes.name: Express Entry: Federal Skilled Worker Program
routes.summary: Permanent residence for skilled workers with foreign or Canadian work experience. No job offer needed, but one can earn points. You also need proof of funds unless you already have a job offer and can work in Canada.

savings.note: For a single applicant. Rises with family size, for example 19,001 CAD for 2 people.

other: One year of continuous work experience in the last 10 years.
Proof of funds is not needed if you are authorized to work in Canada and have a valid job offer.
You are also scored on selection criteria, see the official page.
A provincial nomination adds 600 points.

sources.label: Express Entry: how it works
Express Entry: proof of funds

routes.name: Express Entry: Federal Skilled Trades Program
routes.summary: Permanent residence for people qualified in a skilled trade. You need a full-time job offer or a certificate of qualification.

eligibility.language: CLB 5 for speaking and listening, CLB 4 for reading and writing

savings.note: For a single applicant. Rises with family size. Not needed if you can work in Canada and have a valid job offer.

other: Two years of work experience in the skilled trade in the last 5 years.
Either a full-time job offer of at least one year, or a certificate of qualification.

sources.label: Express Entry: how it works
Express Entry: proof of funds

routes.name: Provincial Nominee Program (PNP)
routes.summary: Provinces and territories nominate people with skills, education or experience they need. Each sets its own streams and rules. Quebec and Nunavut don't run PNP streams.

other: Each province or territory sets its own requirements and nomination numbers.
If you also qualify for a federal Express Entry program, you create an Express Entry profile after nomination, and the nomination adds 600 points.
If you don't qualify for Express Entry, you apply through the separate non-Express Entry process.

sources.label: Immigrate as a provincial nominee

routes.name: Atlantic Immigration Program
routes.summary: Permanent residence for workers with a job offer from a designated employer in New Brunswick, Newfoundland and Labrador, Nova Scotia or Prince Edward Island. Open as of the date checked.

other: Job offer from a designated employer.
Qualifying work experience, unless you recently graduated from a recognized post-secondary school in Atlantic Canada.
Education that fits the job.
Approved language test.
Settlement funds, unless you already live and work in Canada on a valid work permit.
A settlement plan from a service provider organization.

steps: Get a job offer from a designated employer.
Get a settlement plan from a settlement service.
Your employer applies for a provincial endorsement certificate.
Submit your PR application with the certificate.
Apply for a work permit while you wait, if one is required.

sources.label: Atlantic Immigration Program: who can apply
Atlantic Immigration Program: how to immigrate

routes.name: Rural Community Immigration Pilot
routes.summary: Permanent residence for workers with a job offer from a designated employer in a participating rural community. The pilot closes on January 1, 2027, and a permanent program has been announced.

other: Valid recommendation certificate from a participating community. Recommendations dated December 31, 2026 or earlier must still be used before they expire.
Job offer from a designated employer in that community.
At least 1 year (1,560 hours) of related work experience in the past 3 years.
Approved language test, a Canadian education credential or foreign equivalent, and enough settlement funds.
Without a recommendation, see the new Rural Community Immigration Program.

sources.label: Rural Community Immigration Pilot: who can apply

routes.name: Rural Community Immigration Program (permanent)
routes.summary: Announced on November 9, 2026 as the permanent version of the rural pilot. No start date or applicant rules were published on the page read, so check before planning around it.

other: Not open yet as far as the page read shows. Start date and applicant criteria were not given.
The 14 pilot communities are expected to take part. Only employers designated by a community, in its priority sectors, can use it.

sources.label: Overview of the Rural Community Immigration Program

routes.name: Francophone Community Immigration Pilot
routes.summary: Permanent residence for workers with a job offer from a designated employer in a participating Francophone minority community outside Quebec.

other: Valid job offer from a designated employer in the community.
At least 1 year (1,560 hours) of related work experience in the past 3 years.
Approved language test, Canadian education credential or equivalent, and enough settlement funds.
Current open or closed status and community list were not confirmed on the page read.

sources.label: Francophone Community Immigration Pilot: who can apply

routes.name: Employer work permit with LMIA
routes.summary: Most employers need a positive Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMIA) from ESDC before hiring a foreign worker. With the LMIA letter, the worker applies for a work permit tied to that job.

other: A positive LMIA confirms no Canadians or permanent residents are available for the job.
In Quebec, you also need a Quebec Acceptance Certificate (CAQ).
Fees and processing times were not on the page read.

steps: Employer applies for an LMIA.
Employer gives you the positive LMIA letter and Annex A.
You apply for a work permit.

sources.label: Who needs a labour market impact assessment

routes.name: LMIA-exempt work permits (International Mobility Program and Global Skills Strategy)
routes.summary: Some jobs can be filled without an LMIA through the International Mobility Program. The Global Skills Strategy offers faster processing for highly skilled workers.

other: An LMIA exemption code must apply and be included in the job offer.
Workers hired this way don't need a CAQ in Quebec.
Specific exemption categories were not listed on the page read.

sources.label: Who needs a labour market impact assessment

routes.name: International Experience Canada (working holiday and youth work permits)
routes.summary: A work-and-travel program for young people from partner countries. You create a profile, get invited, then apply for a work permit. The 2026 pools are closed and 2027 pools should reopen later.

other: Age limit is 30 for some countries.
Which categories you can use depends on your country, see the official eligibility page.
Fees, permit length and processing time did not load on the page read.

steps: Create an IEC profile.
Get an invitation to apply.
Submit your work permit application.

sources.label: International Experience Canada

routes.name: Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP)
routes.summary: An open work permit for graduates of eligible Canadian programs. Canadian work experience from it can lead to Express Entry.

eligibility.language: CLB 7 for university programs, CLB 5 for college and other programs, in all four skills
other: Program at a PGWP-eligible designated learning institution, at least 8 months long (900 hours in Quebec).
Bachelor's, master's and doctoral graduates have no field-of-study requirement. Other graduates must meet it if their study permit application was submitted on or after November 1, 2024.
Apply within 180 days of confirmation that you completed your program.
Full-time each semester, except the final one.
Permit length was not stated on the page read.

sources.label: Post-graduation work permit: who can apply

routes.name: Study Permit
routes.summary: Permission to study at a Canadian designated learning institution. You need a letter of acceptance, usually a provincial attestation letter, and proof of funds.

savings.note: Living costs for a single applicant, applications on or after September 1, 2026, outside Quebec. Tuition and travel are extra. Higher for families.

other: Letter of acceptance from the school.
Provincial or territorial attestation letter (PAL/TAL) in most cases. Quebec needs a CAQ instead.
Show you can pay first-year tuition and travel to and from Canada.
Fees were not on the pages read.

sources.label: Study permit: get the right documents
Study permit: proof of financial support

routes.name: Start-up Visa Program
routes.summary: Permanent residence for founders backed by a designated organization. It is paused and stopped taking new applications on June 30, 2026. Earlier applications are still being processed.

eligibility.language: CLB 5 in all four skills, English or French

savings.note: Single applicant. Higher for families. Can't be borrowed.

other: Not open to new applications.
Each applicant holds at least 10% of voting rights, and applicants plus the designated organization hold over 50%.
Letter of support and commitment certificate from a designated organization.
Business must be incorporated and managed in Canada after approval.

sources.label: Start-up Visa: who can apply

routes.name: Self-Employed Persons Program
routes.summary: Permanent residence for self-employed people in cultural activities or athletics. It is closed. IRCC stopped accepting applications on April 30, 2024.

other: Closed to new applications.
At least 2 years of cultural or athletic experience, self-employed or at a world-class level.
Must be willing and able to be self-employed in Canada.
Scored on experience, education, age, language and adaptability.
Medical exams, police certificates and enough money to support your family.

sources.label: Self-Employed Persons Program: who can apply

routes.name: Family sponsorship: spouse, partner or dependent child
routes.summary: A Canadian citizen or permanent resident can sponsor a spouse, common-law partner, conjugal partner or dependent child for permanent residence.

other: Spouse: legally married, at least 18, genuine relationship.
Common-law partner: at least 18, lived together at least 12 consecutive months.
Conjugal partner: at least 18, exclusive and interdependent relationship for at least 1 year, living outside Canada and unable to live together or marry for legal or similar reasons.
Dependent child: under 22 with no spouse or partner, or 22 and older if financially dependent since before 22 or unable to support themselves due to a condition.
The relationship must be genuine, not just for immigration. Sponsor requirements, fees and processing times were not on the page read.

sources.label: Sponsor your spouse, partner or children: who you can sponsor

routes.name: Parents and Grandparents Program
routes.summary: Lets citizens and permanent residents sponsor parents and grandparents. It is paused. IRCC isn't accepting interest-to-sponsor forms or issuing invitations until further notice.

other: Paused as of the page update on August 18, 2026. Existing applications are still processed.
When open: submit an interest-to-sponsor form, wait for an invitation, then apply.
Income rules and fees were not on the page read.

sources.label: Sponsor your parents and grandparents

routes.name: Super Visa for parents and grandparents
routes.summary: A long-stay visitor visa for parents and grandparents of Canadian citizens and permanent residents. You can stay up to 5 years at a time.

other: Host must meet the minimum necessary income. The amount was not on the page read.
Private health insurance valid at least one year from entry, from a Canadian insurer or an approved foreign one.
Immigration medical exam.
If you plan to stay 6 months or less, a regular visitor visa may do.

stay.note: Up to 5 years at a time, with 2-year extensions possible from inside Canada.

sources.label: Super visa: who can apply

routes.name: Home Care Worker Immigration Pilots (caregivers)
routes.summary: Permanent residence for home child care providers and home support workers. The pilots are closed to new applications while IRCC processes existing ones.

eligibility.education: Canadian high school diploma or higher (foreign credentials need assessment)
other: Closed to new applications.
Either 6 months of continuous full-time relevant experience in the past 3 years, or a relevant training credential completed in the past 2 years.
Live and work outside Quebec.
The Workers in Canada stream needs full-time non-seasonal work authorization. The stream for applicants outside Canada is closed and will open later.

sources.label: Home Care Worker Immigration pilots: eligibility

routes.name: Asylum (refugee protection claim)
routes.summary: You can claim asylum from inside Canada or at the border if you meet the definition of a Convention refugee or person in need of protection. Start online in the IRCC Portal. The Immigration and Refugee Board decides at a hearing.

other: Some circumstances make a claim ineligible. See the official page.
IRCC changed the process on November 3, 2026. Unsubmitted portal claims need new questions answered.
Resettlement from outside Canada is a separate process not covered here.

steps: Start your claim in the IRCC Portal.
Complete the claim and submit evidence.
Eligibility interview with IRCC or CBSA.
Hearing at the Refugee Protection Division of the IRB.
Receive the decision.

sources.label: Claiming asylum in Canada

routes.name: Canadian citizenship by naturalization (permanent residents)
routes.summary: Permanent residents can apply after being physically in Canada at least 1,095 days in the last 5 years. Adults 18 to 54 need basic English or French and a citizenship test.

eligibility.language: CLB or NCLC 4 in speaking and listening (ages 18 to 54)
other: At least 1,095 days in Canada in the 5 years before you sign, with at least 730 of them as a permanent resident. Days as a temporary resident or protected person count as half days, up to 365 days.
Filed Canadian taxes for at least 3 of the 5 years, if required.
Citizenship test for ages 18 to 54 and oath ceremony.
Criminal or security issues can block approval.
Marrying a Canadian does not make you a citizen automatically.

citizenship.note: Canada allows dual citizenship, but your other country may not. Check with its embassy.

sources.label: Become a Canadian citizen: eligibility

routes.name: Citizenship by descent (after Bill C-3)
routes.summary: Bill C-3 took effect December 15, 2025 and extended citizenship by descent beyond the first generation. A parent born or adopted abroad now needs 1,095 days (3 years) in Canada before your birth or adoption.

other: Before the change, descent was limited to the first generation born abroad.
Now second and later generations can qualify, and remaining Lost Canadians and their descendants are covered.

For people born or adopted abroad on or after December 15, 2025 to a Canadian parent who was also born or adopted abroad, the parent needs at least 1,095 days of cumulative physical presence in Canada before the birth or adoption.
People born before December 15, 2025 who became citizens automatically can apply for proof of citizenship.
The page did not detail the rules for those born before the change, so check the official guidance for your family line.

citizenship.note: Canada allows dual citizenship. Your other country's rules may differ.
